  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Jose Covarrubias, Facility Maintenance Supervisor
Date:  March 26, 2026

Subject:  Park Facility Maintenance Division Annual Report

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary:
The following is a report on what The Park Facilities Division has performed and
accomplished during the past year.

This Division has successfully hosted, organized, and facilitated a wide array of events
throughout the year. This includes both recurring City sponsored events, such as Winter
Wonderland, Christmas Parade, Breakfast with Santa, Rotary Thanksgiving dinner, and
community focused events like facility and picnic reservations, sports activities, food
giveaways, blood drives, job fairs, and various educational classes. Our team has
demonstrated adaptability and efficiency in supporting these events, ensuring their
smooth execution from setup to teardown.

To enhance our operational capabilities, we invested in new disinfecting equipment,
including portable disinfectant sprayers, floor auto-scrubbing machines, and portable
pressure washers. These additions have significantly improved our ability to maintain
cleanliness and hygiene across both indoor and outdoor park facilities, ensuring the
safety and comfort of all park users.

Additionally, we installed privacy walls at Hollydale Reginal Park men’s restroom near
the tennis courts. This improvement is addressing public safety concerns.

The Community Service Worker Program has been instrumental in supporting the
Facilities Division. Currently, the program is accepting up to fifteen volunteers to assist
with Facility and Grounds Maintenance staff, with the potential to expand the number of
volunteers as needed. This program has provided valuable support, contributing to the
overall efficiency and upkeep of our facilities.

To accommodate the growing number of classes, reservations, and events, staff
schedules have been adjusted to ensure full coverage and support. Facility staff have

Subject:  Review of Concession Agreements
Recommended Motion:  Motion to Receive and File
Report Summary: Each year the Commission reviews the Department’s current concession
agreements and provides staff with recommendations, particularly for those agreements that are
currently up for extension or renewal. Typically, agreements are those that allow a private
business, either for profit or non-profit, to conduct business on Park property or to operate a
program on behalf of the City.
Below is a list of the concession agreements that are currently active along with information
regarding their expiration dates.
Overall, we are happy with the current providers and are not recommending any major changes

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 5
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Tina De La Rosa, Interim Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  March 10, 2026
Subject:  Proposed Renaming of Cesar Chavez Park

Recommended Motion:  Suggest new names for Cesar Chavez Park and submit to
Council for their review.

Report Summary: In light of recent allegations that have brought renewed public
attention and concern, the City has taken a proactive step to remove the name from the
park out of sensitivity to community sentiment. As stewards of our public spaces, it is
important that our park names reflect values that unify our community and ensure that
all residents feel comfortable and welcome in these shared environments.

As part of this process, City Council is asking the Parks and Recreation Commission to
provide three to five potential name recommendations that can be presented to the City
Council at the next meeting.
